headline: An OCSP response is no longer signed with a status window that runs backwards.
summary: pki.ocsp.sign accepted a SingleResponse whose thisUpdate fell after its nextUpdate and signed it, so a responder could hand a relying party a status window that closed before it opened. pki.ocsp.verify reports such a response unknown, so the response was unusable rather than misleading, but every other signing verb in the toolkit already refuses its own reversed window. It now refuses too.

Fixed: pki.ocsp.sign raises ocsp/bad-input for a response entry whose thisUpdate is after its nextUpdate, before anything is signed. RFC 6960 section 4.2.2.1 makes the pair a validity interval corresponding to the {thisUpdate, nextUpdate} interval in CRLs, and pki.crl.sign, pki.x509.sign, pki.attrcert.sign and pki.crmf.sign each already refuse their own reversed window. Every entry in a batch is measured, not the first alone, and the times are checked as they will be encoded, so a defaulted nextUpdate is held to the rule a supplied one is.
An entry whose thisUpdate equals its nextUpdate still signs, as the equivalent CRL does: a zero-length window is not forbidden. A response entry that names no certificate still reports that first.

A pre-produced response still signs. RFC 6960 section 2.5 lets a responder sign a response ahead of the window it certifies, where producedAt is when the response was signed and thisUpdate is when the status was known correct, so a producedAt earlier than thisUpdate is conforming and is left alone.
